name: The Sun: Our Star
teaser: The glowing heart of our solar system

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what makes the Sun a star and how its energy is made, then explain why it looks yellow and what will happen to it in five billion years.

name: What the Sun Is Made Of
teaser: A giant ball of glowing gas

exploreAction.targetName: Find out what the Sun is made of
exploreAction.instruction: Find out what the Sun is mostly made of and how nuclear fusion works in its core, then explain why it shines steadily instead of exploding.
Explore the Sun's layers from the core out to the corona, then explain why the corona is hotter than the surface and what that mystery suggests.

name: Sunspots and Solar Storms
teaser: Dark spots on the Sun's face

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how sunspots form and how solar flares and coronal mass ejections affect Earth, then explain what auroras have to do with them.

name: The Solar Wind
teaser: A stream of particles from the Sun

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the solar wind and how it shapes the solar system, then explain how it creates comet tails and the heliosphere.

name: The Sun's Life Cycle
teaser: A star from birth to white dwarf

exploreAction.instruction: Follow the Sun's life from a collapsing cloud to a red giant to a white dwarf, then explain why it will not explode as a supernova.

name: Solar Eclipses
teaser: When the Moon covers the Sun

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how and why solar eclipses happen and why they are rare at any one spot, then explain the difference between total, partial and annular eclipses.
Find out why a lunar eclipse turns the Moon red and why they are easier to see than solar eclipses, then explain the geometry behind them.
Learn how Earth's axial tilt creates the seasons, then explain why summer and winter are opposite in the two hemispheres.

name: Equinoxes and Solstices
teaser: The turning points of the year

exploreAction.instruction: Find out what an equinox and a solstice are and when they happen each year, then explain how different cultures have marked them.

name: Zodiacal Light
teaser: A faint glow in the twilight sky

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the faint zodiacal light that appears before dawn, then explain what causes it and when and where it is best seen.
Learn what a supermoon is and why the Moon sometimes looks bigger and brighter, then explain why the change is easy to overestimate.
Find out what a blue moon really is and why the phrase is misleading, then explain how often they appear.
Learn why the Moon appears to change shape over a month, then explain the difference between waxing and waning and what a new moon is.
Discover how the Moon's gravity creates ocean tides and why there are two high tides a day, then explain what spring and neap tides are.

name: Why the Moon Looks Big at the Horizon
teaser: An illusion, not a real change

exploreAction.instruction: Investigate why the Moon looks enormous near the horizon and small overhead, then explain the illusion that tricks your brain.

name: The Far Side of the Moon

exploreAction.instruction: Find out why we always see the same face of the Moon and what the far side looks like, then explain the difference between the dark side and the far side.
Learn the leading theory of how the Moon formed from a giant impact, then explain the evidence that supports it.

name: Lunar Regolith
teaser: The dusty skin of the Moon

exploreAction.instruction: Discover what lunar regolith is and how it formed, then explain why moon dust is sharp and why it was a problem for Apollo.
Find out what moonquakes are and what triggers them, then explain how they differ from earthquakes on Earth.
Learn why Mercury has the wildest temperature swings in the solar system, then explain how a day on Mercury can last two Mercury years.

name: Seeing Mercury and Venus in Phases
teaser: Like tiny moons in a telescope

exploreAction.instruction: Find out why Mercury and Venus show phases like the Moon, then explain how observing them helped Galileo prove the planets orbit the Sun.

name: Venus: The Cloud World
teaser: A bright planet wrapped in clouds

exploreAction.instruction: Discover why Venus is the hottest planet even though Mercury is closer to the Sun, then explain the runaway greenhouse effect.

name: Venus's Crushing Atmosphere
teaser: Ninety times the pressure of Earth's

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what the atmosphere of Venus is made of and why it crushes spacecraft, then explain the sulfuric acid clouds and lightning.

name: Venus Spins Backward
teaser: A planet that turns the wrong way

exploreAction.instruction: Find out why Venus rotates backward and so slowly, then explain what a day and a year mean there.

name: Olympus Mons
teaser: The tallest volcano in the solar system

exploreAction.instruction: Discover Olympus Mons and why it grew so enormous, then explain how Mars could once have had erupting volcanoes.

name: Valles Marineris
teaser: A canyon that would stretch across the USA

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about Valles Marineris and how it formed, then explain why it dwarfs Earth's Grand Canyon.

name: Water on Mars
teaser: Rivers and lakes that dried up

exploreAction.instruction: Investigate the evidence that Mars once had rivers, lakes and oceans, then explain where that water went.

name: Mars's Polar Caps
teaser: Ice at the red planet's poles

exploreAction.instruction: Find out what the polar caps of Mars are made of and how they change with the seasons, then explain why they matter for future missions.

name: Phobos: The Doomed Moon
teaser: A moon that will crash into Mars

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about Phobos and why it is slowly spiraling toward Mars, then explain when it will break apart or crash.

name: Deimos: A Tiny Companion
teaser: The smaller, quieter moon of Mars

name: Jupiter's Magnetic Field
teaser: The strongest magnet in the solar system

exploreAction.instruction: Find out how Jupiter's magnetic field works and why it is so strong, then explain what causes its enormous auroras.
Discover why Io is covered in active volcanoes, then explain the tidal heating that fuels them.
Learn about Europa's subsurface ocean and the evidence for it, then explain why scientists think it could host life.
Discover Ganymede, the largest moon in the solar system, then explore its magnetic field and possible underground ocean.

name: Callisto: The Cratered Relic
teaser: A moon that records ancient impacts

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why Callisto is so heavily cratered and what its ancient surface tells us, then explain why it is a candidate for a future base.
Discover that Jupiter has rings and why they are hard to see, then explain how they are created and sustained.

name: Saturn's Rings
teaser: The jewel of the solar system

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what Saturn's rings are made of and how wide they stretch, then explain why they are so thin and bright.

exploreAction.targetName: Find out where the rings came from
exploreAction.instruction: Investigate the leading ideas for how Saturn's rings formed, then explain why they may be much younger than the planet.
Discover why Saturn is the least dense planet and whether it could really float, then explain what that reveals about its interior.
Discover Titan's lakes, rivers and rain made of methane, then explain why it is seen as one of the best places to look for life.

name: Enceladus's Geysers
teaser: Plumes of water from a tiny moon

exploreAction.instruction: Learn about the geysers of Enceladus and the ocean beneath its ice, then explain what the Cassini mission found in the plumes.

name: Mimas and the Death Star

Discover the icy moons Tethys and Rhea and their surprising features, then explain how scientists map them without landing.

name: Uranus: The Tilted Planet
teaser: A world that rolls around the Sun

exploreAction.instruction: Learn why Uranus spins on its side and how its seasons work, then explain what may have knocked it over.

name: Neptune's Supersonic Winds

name: Why Pluto Is a Dwarf Planet

name: Ceres: The Asteroid Queen
teaser: The largest object in the asteroid belt

name: The Kuiper Belt
teaser: A ring of icy worlds beyond Neptune

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what the Kuiper Belt is and what lives there, then explain how Pluto relates to it.

name: The Oort Cloud
teaser: A shell of comets around the solar system

exploreAction.instruction: Discover the Oort Cloud and why no one has seen it directly, then explain how it sends comets toward the Sun.

name: The Asteroid Belt
teaser: A ring of rubble between Mars and Jupiter

exploreAction.instruction: Learn what the asteroid belt is and why it never formed into a planet, then explain how big its largest members are.

name: Types of Asteroids
teaser: C, S and M — the cosmic building blocks

name: Planetary Defense

name: Meteorites
teaser: Rocks that fall from the sky

exploreAction.instruction: Learn the difference between meteors, meteoroids and meteorites, then explain what meteorites tell us about the early solar system.

name: Shooting Stars
teaser: Why meteors flash across the sky

exploreAction.instruction: Find out what a shooting star really is and why it glows, then explain the difference between a meteor and a satellite streak.

name: The Leonid Meteor Storms
teaser: When meteors fall by the thousands

name: Why Comets Have Tails

name: The Heart of a Comet
teaser: A dirty snowball at the center

name: Bolides and Fireballs

name: White Dwarfs

teaser: The invisible mass holding galaxies together

teaser: The afterglow of the Big Bang

name: The Cosmic Web
teaser: Galaxies arranged in filaments and voids

name: The Fine-Tuning Question
teaser: Why the universe's constants are just right

name: Echoes of Inflation

name: The Milky Way

name: Cosmic Dust

name: The Milky Way's Mergers

teaser: A tool that opened the universe

teaser: The blurry first images and the daring fix

name: The James Webb Space Telescope
teaser: The most powerful space telescope ever

exploreAction.instruction: Learn how JWST sees the infrared and why it orbits far from Earth, then explain what its deep images reveal.

name: Webb vs Hubble

name: The Keck Telescopes

name: Adaptive Optics
teaser: Fixing the blur of the atmosphere

exploreAction.instruction: Discover how adaptive optics removes atmospheric blur in real time, then explain how it made ground telescopes sharper.

name: Light Pollution
teaser: The sky glow that hides the stars

name: Naked-Eye Astronomy
teaser: What you can see without a telescope

Learn how amateur astronomers contribute real discoveries, then explain what equipment you actually need to start.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus

name: Johannes Kepler

teaser: The law that explains the orbits

name: Vera Rubin

name: Stephen Hawking

name: Harlow Shapley

name: Early Planet Hunters

name: Curiosity on Mars
